identity.name: Internet-Exposed Attack-Surface Discovery & Enumeration (T1595 / T1046 / T1190)
identity.summary: A deliberately exposed public host (nginx dir-listing, weak self-signed RSA-1024 TLS, SSH on 2222 with password auth, unauthenticated Redis on 6379, a vulnerable ES 1.7.0 banner on 9200, gocortexbrokenbank on 9001) plus a public S3 website are scanned with nmap + nuclei. Cortex ASM/Xpanse discovers and enumerates the exposed surface; NGFW logs the active-scanning egress shape.
identity.description: Adversaries begin most intrusions with active scanning (T1595) of internet-facing assets to enumerate open ports, service banners, weak TLS, and exploitable public-facing applications (T1190). CortexSim provisions a predictable target set via the infra/modules/aws/asm Terraform module: one Ubuntu 22.04 host in the public subnet exposing nginx directory listing + bait files on :80, weak self-signed RSA-1024 TLS on :443, SSH on the non-standard :2222 with password auth, an unauthenticated/world-bound Redis on :6379, a fake Elasticsearch 1.7.0 banner on :9200, and the intentionally vulnerable gocortexbrokenbank app on :9001 — plus a separate public S3 static-website bucket. The DC runs nmap (port + service/version enumeration, T1046) and nuclei (template-driven exposure/misconfig/CVE scanning, T1595/T1190) against the host. This card validates the exposure-management surface in three layers: (1) a ground-truth manifest XQL that confirms the planted CortexSimASMFinding-tagged resources exist in the cloud inventory; (2) Cortex ASM/Xpanse discovery findings from asm_assets/asm_findings showing each exposed port, the short-RSA self-signed cert, the non-standard SSH port, the known-vulnerable ES 1.7.0 banner, the directory-listing nginx root, and the public S3 website endpoint; and (3) an NGFW traffic BIOC/XQL that detects the active-scanning egress shape (one source fanning out across many ports/templates) so the SOC can correlate the discovery findings with the scan that surfaced them. A correlation rule fuses the ASM exposure findings with the active-scan signal into a single exposure-management incident, and IOC signatures pin the exposed-service fingerprints (ES 1.7.0 banner, RSA-1024 self-signed CN, world-bound Redis port) that ASM attack-path recommendations should prioritise.

execution.framework_reference_id: T1595 / T1046 / T1190 — nmap service-version sweep + nuclei exposure templates against the infra/modules/aws/asm exposed host

prerequisites.description: infra/modules/aws/asm bundle applied; the exposed multi-service EC2 host has a reachable public IP and the public S3 website bucket exists.
Cortex ASM/Xpanse is configured to scan the customer perimeter that includes the exposed host, and NGFW egress traffic from the jumpbox is forwarded to XSIAM (panw_ngfw_traffic_raw).

payload.code:
# step-1: nmap full service+version enumeration of the exposed host (T1046)
nmap -sS -sV -Pn -T4 -p 80,443,2222,6379,9001,9200 -oX /tmp/nmap-cortexsim-asm.xml ${ASM_TARGET_HOST}
# step-2: nuclei template-driven exposure/misconfig/CVE scan (T1595/T1190)
nuclei -target http://${ASM_TARGET_HOST} -severity medium,high,critical -t exposures,misconfigurations,cves -o /tmp/nuclei-cortexsim.json -j -rate-limit 150
# step-3: probe the unauthenticated services that ASM should flag
redis-cli -h ${ASM_TARGET_HOST} -p 6379 INFO server 2>/dev/null | head -5 || true
curl -sk https://${ASM_TARGET_HOST}:9200/ | head -1 || true

input_variables.name: ASM_TARGET_HOST
input_variables.description: Public IP / hostname of the infra/modules/aws/asm exposed EC2 instance.

expected_artifacts.description: A single source enumerating many distinct ports on the exposed host in a short window (active-scan fan-out).
expected_artifacts.expected_value: count_distinct(dst_port) per src_ip >= 5 against the exposed host

expected_artifacts.description: Outbound web-app probing traffic from nuclei against the exposed host on :80/:443/:9001/:9200.
Cortex ASM/Xpanse discovery findings enumerate each exposed service, the weak TLS cert and the public S3 website.

iocs.context: Known end-of-life / vulnerable Elasticsearch version banner returned by the exposed :9200 service — ASM should CVE-match and prioritise this exposure.
Self-signed RSA-1024 TLS certificate served on :443 — short-key/self-signed weak-TLS exposure signature ASM should surface.
Unauthenticated, world-bound Redis (protected-mode off) — high-severity exposed-data-store signature.

biocs.name: ASM EAL — Active-Scan Port Fan-Out Against Exposed Host
biocs.description: A single source IP opens connections to an unusually large number of distinct destination ports on the exposed surface host within a short window — the nmap/nuclei active-scanning egress shape (T1595/T1046).
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter dst_port in (80, 443, 2222, 6379, 9001, 9200) or app in ("web-browsing", "ssl", "redis", "elasticsearch")
| filter src_ip != null and dst_ip != null
| bin _time span=5m
| comp count_distinct(dst_port) as scanned_ports, count() as session_count by src_ip, dst_ip, _time
| filter scanned_ports >= 5
| fields _time, src_ip, dst_ip, scanned_ports, session_count

xql_queries.name: ASM-001 Ground-Truth Manifest Capture Bookkeeping
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter cloud_provider = "AWS"
| filter resource_tags contains "CortexSimASMFinding"
| comp count_distinct(resource_id) as planted_resources by resource_type
| fields resource_type, planted_resources

xql_queries.name: ASM Exposed-Service Discovery Findings By Port
xql_queries.query:
dataset = asm_findings
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter finding_type in ("exposed_service", "open_port", "weak_tls", "non_standard_port", "public_cloud_storage")
| filter tags contains "CortexSimASMFinding" or asset_external_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}"
| comp count() as findings by finding_type, service_port, service_name
| fields finding_type, service_port, service_name, findings

xql_queries.name: ASM EAL — Active-Scan Port Fan-Out (1 src to many ports on exposed host)
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter dst_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}"
| filter dst_port in (80, 443, 2222, 6379, 9001, 9200)
| comp count_distinct(dst_port) as scanned_ports, count() as sessions by src_ip, dst_ip
| filter scanned_ports >= 5
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, scanned_ports, sessions

xql_queries.name: ASM High-Risk Exposure Roll-Up — Weak TLS, EOL Banner, Unauth Data Store
xql_queries.query:
dataset = asm_findings
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400)
| filter (finding_type = "weak_tls" and (tls_key_bits <= 1024 or tls_self_signed = true))
    or (finding_type = "vulnerable_service" and service_version contains "1.7.0")
    or (finding_type = "exposed_service" and service_name in ("redis", "elasticsearch") and service_auth = "none")
| comp count() as high_risk_findings by finding_type, service_name, service_version, risk_score
| sort desc risk_score
| fields finding_type, service_name, service_version, risk_score, high_risk_findings

correlation_rules.name: Exposure Management — Internet-Exposed Surface Discovered + Actively Scanned
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(ASM Exposed-Service Discovery Findings By Port) AND (BIOC(ASM EAL — Active-Scan Port Fan-Out Against Exposed Host) OR XQL(ASM EAL — Active-Scan Port Fan-Out (1 src to many ports on exposed host))) — raises a single exposure-management incident tying the discovered exposed services to the active scan that surfaced them.

analytics_modules: Cortex Xpanse / ASM — Attack Surface Discovery and Service Enumeration
Cortex Xpanse / ASM — Attack-Path Risk Prioritisation (weak TLS, EOL banner, unauthenticated data store)
Cortex XSIAM Network Security Analytics — Outbound Active-Scan Port Fan-Out

products.evidence_query: dataset = asm_findings | filter finding_type in ("exposed_service","weak_tls","public_cloud_storage") | comp count() by finding_type, service_port
dataset = asm_findings | filter asset_external_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}" | comp count() by service_port, service_name
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw | filter dst_ip = "${ASM_TARGET_HOST}" | comp count_distinct(dst_port) as ports by src_ip | filter ports >= 5

Playbook: open exposure-management ticket per finding, recommend closing the non-standard SSH port, removing world-bound Redis, replacing the weak self-signed cert, and restricting the public S3 website policy.

use_cases.name: Attack Surface Discovery & Enumeration via Cortex ASM
use_cases.description: Validate that Cortex ASM/Xpanse discovers and enumerates a deliberately exposed public host + public S3 website, prioritises the high-risk exposures, and that NGFW telemetry detects the active scan that surfaced them.

test_cases.objective: Cortex ASM discovers and enumerates every exposed service on the host plus the public S3 website.
preconditions: infra/modules/aws/asm bundle applied with a reachable public IP.
Cortex ASM scanning the perimeter that includes the exposed host.
steps: Inspect Cortex ASM / asm_findings for the exposed-service findings.
success_criteria: XQL `ASM Exposed-Service Discovery Findings By Port` returns >= 1 row covering the exposed ports.
Cortex ASM surfaces the non-standard SSH port, the weak TLS cert, and the public S3 website endpoint.

test_cases.objective: The active scan that surfaced the exposures is detected and correlated into one exposure-management incident.
steps: Inspect Network Security Analytics and the correlation incident.
success_criteria: XQL `ASM EAL — Active-Scan Port Fan-Out (1 src to many ports on exposed host)` returns >= 1 row with scanned_ports >= 5.
Correlation `CR-ASM-0001` raises a single exposure-management incident tying discovery findings to the scan.
XQL `ASM High-Risk Exposure Roll-Up — Weak TLS, EOL Banner, Unauth Data Store` returns >= 1 high-risk row.

preventive_controls: Remove internet exposure of management/data services: bind Redis to localhost with auth + protected-mode on, and never expose Elasticsearch directly.
Run SSH on the standard port behind a bastion, disable password auth in favour of key-based auth, and restrict source CIDRs.
Replace self-signed / short-RSA certificates with CA-issued >= 2048-bit (preferably ECDSA) certificates and disable legacy TLS versions and directory listing.
Restrict the public S3 bucket policy and disable static-website hosting unless required; front public web content with a CDN/WAF.
detection_engineering: Continuously run Cortex ASM/Xpanse perimeter discovery and alert on net-new exposed services, non-standard ports, weak TLS, and end-of-life service banners.
Baseline per-source destination-port cardinality at the NGFW and alert on active-scan fan-out against perimeter assets.
Stitch ASM exposure findings with the active-scan NGFW signal so the SOC sees one exposure-management incident, not isolated findings.
Tag intentional lab targets so ground-truth manifest reconciliation can confirm full discovery coverage.
